chixoy-rio-negro.conditions_add: The Bank's appraisal of the Chixoy Power Project sets out what the Government and the state electricity utility INDE had to do for Loan 1605-GU. They had to compensate and, where necessary, resettle the roughly 1,500 people affected by the reservoir, and INDE had to submit that programme to the Bank by 31 December 1979, together with an erosion control programme the Government was to start carrying out by 30 June 1980. The loan also turned on electricity prices: it could not become effective until the Government confirmed tariff increases large enough to give the sector a 13 percent internal contribution to investment in 1978, from 1980 retail tariffs had to earn an 8 percent return on revalued net fixed assets, fuel price rises passed automatically to consumers, and tariffs could not be cut before the project was finished without the Bank's agreement (World Bank, Staff Appraisal Report, 1978).

why.safeguard: compensate and, where necessary, resettle the roughly 1,500 people affected by the reservoir
why.prices: fuel price rises passed automatically to consumers
why.fincov: retail tariffs had to earn an 8 percent return on revalued net fixed assets

kainji-dam.conditions_add: The Bank's 1964 appraisal records that the loan would not become effective until agreements for the equivalent of US$45 million of other foreign loans had been signed on terms acceptable to the Bank. The Niger Dams Authority had to earn revenues giving at least an 8 percent return on its average net fixed assets in operation, could take on no long-term debt during construction without the Bank's agreement and from 1969 only if net revenues covered debt service 1.5 times, had to be audited each year by accountants acceptable to the Bank, and could not have a chief executive whose qualifications the Bank had not accepted. No new generating plant for the interconnected system could be built before Kainji was fully developed without the Bank's approval, and the Federal Government had to provide any further funds needed to finish the works on terms satisfactory to the Bank (World Bank, Staff Appraisal Report, Kainji Multipurpose Project, 1964). The appraisal sets out no Bank covenant on the resettlement of the roughly 40,000-140,000 people the reservoir displaced, only a budget line for compensation and resettlement.

why.fincov: revenues giving at least an 8 percent return on its average net fixed assets in operation
why.admin: could not have a chief executive whose qualifications the Bank had not accepted

pak-mun.conditions_add: The Bank's 1991 appraisal of the Third Power System Development Project, which financed Pak Mun, lists the agreements reached with the Electricity Generating Authority of Thailand. EGAT was to carry out a resettlement and rehabilitation plan satisfactory to the Bank, offering affected families either at least 0.08 hectares for a house plot and 1.6 hectares of farmland or houses rebuilt on backfilled ground; a fisheries development plan satisfactory to the Bank, with a fisheries conservation unit, fish migration studies and the construction and monitoring of a fish ladder for migratory fish; a plan satisfactory to the Bank for preventing and monitoring endemic disease; and a site management plan satisfactory to the Bank covering construction runoff, spoil areas, archaeological sites and farmland. EGAT also agreed to appoint a board of three consultants to review design and construction and to keep the environmental, mitigation and resettlement reports open for public inspection at its offices (World Bank, Staff Appraisal Report, 1991).

jakarta-water-1997.conditions_add: The appraisal of the Second Jabotabek Urban Development Project, which carried the loan to PAM Jaya, made two things conditions of loan effectiveness: satisfactory subsidiary loan agreements between the central government and PDAM Jaya, DKI Jakarta and PDAM Tangerang, and the appointment of key staff (division manager, financial accountant and monitoring officer) to the project coordination office. The project's financial arrangements included a cash flow covenant requiring a contribution towards capital expenditure, a review and adjustment of water tariffs at least every three years rather than every five, and agreement by the Jakarta and Tangerang authorities to let their water utilities keep and reinvest their share of profits; the utility also agreed to let all households sell water on to neighbours and water vendors (World Bank, Staff Appraisal Report, 1990). Nothing in the appraisal required the utility to be privatised.

plantar-minas-gerais.conditions_add: The World Bank's project information document for the Prototype Carbon Fund's Plantar project says the Fund buys emission reductions under a purchase agreement with Plantar S.A. that sets the quantity, price and other delivery conditions together with the monitoring and verification protocols, and that "payments will only be effected on an annual basis after monitoring and verification" of the reductions achieved; the Fund buys only certified reductions and does not finance project components. kpone-landfill-tema.conditions_add: The credit set conditions before work could start on the waste sites. Before building the Tema sanitary landfill or improving, closing or rehabilitating the dumps at Mallam, Oblogo, Kpone and Essipon, the borrower had to prepare and carry out a Resettlement Action Plan satisfactory to the Bank under the project's Resettlement Policy Framework and acquire all the land needed, and the appraisal states that "the acquisition of land for the sanitary landfills is a condition of disbursement". The same works also required an Environmental Management Plan satisfactory to the Bank beforehand. The credit itself could not take effect until an external auditor had been appointed and a Project Implementation Manual adopted, and the ministry had to appoint a project manager, engineer, training specialist and accountant by 30 November 2004 (World Bank, Project Appraisal Document, 2004).

bhabadah-waterlogging-kjdrp.conditions_add: The ADB loan carried 43 covenants. Three of them required the government to coordinate project activities at divisional and district level through meetings chaired by the commissioner, to obtain the agreement of at least 90 percent of farmers in a polder area before shrimp culture there, and to implement, operate and maintain the project in a way consistent with the country’s own environmental standards (ADB Project Performance Evaluation Report, Loan 1289-BAN(SF), 2007). The evaluation found all three were not met.
